title: Refill No leaked resource after SQL cancel for issue53843 ADD INDEX local ingest

payload.validation_scope: SQL-level ADD INDEX cancel active-write window with direct backend resource observers. Current master is GREEN with no live mock ingest resources; vulnerable cc127c14 is RED with duplicate cleanup ownership on the same observed backend context.
payload.scope_caveat: Validated only for the narrowed SQL-cancel terminal-resource obligation. The broad oracle.no-leak-after-cancel.v1 remains hypothesis until stronger live/local-backend observers prove real file/writer leakage behavior.

name: DDL ingest SQL cancel must leave no live local ingest resource

payload.p_check: ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS or an equivalent rollback/cancel path reaches ADD INDEX local ingest after BackendCtx.Register has opened at least one engine or writer.
payload.q_claim: When cancel/rollback becomes terminal, every resource registered by that job is terminal and cleanup ownership for the job's backend context is exactly once.
payload.fault_model: Cancel lands after local engine registration and before natural FinishAndUnregisterEngines completion; the harness must prove the active-resource window was hit before accepting a verdict.
source_anchors: pkg/ddl/ingest/backend_mgr.go:295-304 vulnerable manager-side Unregister calls bc.UnregisterEngines()
current pkg/ddl/backfilling.go closes or cleans engines through a single FinishAndUnregisterEngines path
payload.stop_rule: Record INVALID(harness), not GREEN, if the cancel does not hit after local engine registration or resource observers are unavailable.
payload.scope_caveat: This validation proves the narrowed SQL cancel cleanup-ownership obligation. It does not by itself validate every consumer of the broad no-leak-after-cancel oracle.

name: DDL ingest cancel reaches terminal state with no live backend resource

payload.contract: For an ADD INDEX local-ingest job cancelled after active resource registration, terminal job observation must imply no live ingest backend resource remains and no backend cleanup ownership is exercised more than once.
payload.narrows: Scoped to ADD INDEX local ingest SQL cancel with direct resource ownership observers, not only SQL job state.
red_signature: terminal job with live_engine_count > 0 or live_writer_count > 0
same backend context cleanup owner count > 1
same engine UUID is closed twice
invalid_signature: no proof that ADD INDEX reached local-ingest engine registration
cancel delivered after the pipeline already finished
payload.scope_caveat: Keep oracle.no-leak-after-cancel.v1 as hypothesis; this narrow oracle is execution-verified only for the SQL ADD INDEX cancel terminal-resource case.

name: SQL cancel after local ingest engine opens

trigger_condition.phase: after backend context registration and at least one active mock writer row write
trigger_condition.required_evidence: jobID plus active_resource_window_hit, such as registered>0 and writes>0

payload.fault_action: Issue ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS for the active job, or inject the same rollback/cancel transition, while backend resources are live.
payload.observer_action: After terminal cancel/rollback, sample backend resource counters and cleanup-owner counters for the job.
invalid_if: the hold fires before local engines are registered
the job reaches terminal state before cancel
observer cannot map resources back to the jobID
payload.scope_caveat: The vulnerable RED used an observing mock backend manager to expose old litBackendCtxMgr cleanup semantics. This validates the schedule/fault shape for SQL-level cleanup ownership, not a full live local-file leak replay.
